title: OverlayManager: mount lazy overlays only when open (prevent eager imports)
description:
## Problem
`React.lazy(...)` only buys us code-splitting **if the lazy component is not mounted**.

Right now, `OverlayManager` renders all lazy overlay components unconditionally, even when they are not in the open overlay stack. In practice this can:
- trigger eager dynamic imports and network fetches for overlay chunks on cold start
- increase parse/compile work at startup
- increase memory usage (overlay code in RAM)
- undermine the “true lazy overlays” goal of Phase 7

### Evidence / where to look
- `packages/web/src/components/overlays/OverlayManager.tsx` (previously observed around ~L116) renders the overlay components regardless of the overlay stack.

## Root cause
The render tree includes *all* `React.lazy` overlay components. Mounting a `React.lazy` component is enough to schedule/trigger its module load.

## Goal
Keep overlays truly lazy-loaded:
- overlay bundles must not be imported/fetched until the overlay is opened
- global overlay-open hotkeys must still work immediately after app load

## Proposed approach
1) Render only what is open
- Drive overlay rendering from the overlay stack (e.g., `overlayStack.map(({ id }) => <LazyOverlayForId id={id} ... />)`).
- Do **not** mount overlays that are not currently open.

2) Keep global overlay-open hotkeys shell-level
- Global hotkeys must not require overlay mount. This is the core invariant of `phage_explorer-s4qx.2`.

3) Optional: intentional preloading (not implicit)
If we want “instant first open” without breaking lazy-load:
- add an explicit `preloadOverlay(OverlayId)` API that can be called from:
  - menu hover/focus
  - after initial idle (`requestIdleCallback`)
  - explicit “prefetch overlays” setting

4) Guardrails
- Ensure React Strict Mode / double-render behavior does not accidentally cause imports.
- Ensure overlay Suspense fallbacks are only used when an overlay is opened.

## Testing plan (must)
### E2E (Playwright)
- Add a deterministic network assertion test that fails if any overlay chunks are requested on cold load.
- After opening a specific overlay, assert that overlay’s chunk is fetched and unrelated overlays remain unfetched.

Use:
- `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.4` for the automated test, and
- `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.1` for structured logging artifacts.

### Manual verification (supporting)
- `phage_explorer-s4qx.2.4` should document the human verification steps (DevTools Network + expected behavior).

## Acceptance criteria
- Cold load: **no overlay chunks** are fetched until an overlay is opened.
- Opening an overlay fetches only that overlay’s chunk(s) + shared chunks.
- Overlay-open hotkeys still work immediately after first load.
- No behavior regression in overlay stacking / close / focus.
- Automated e2e coverage prevents chunking regressions.

## Notes
- This work intentionally blocks `phage_explorer-s4qx.2.4` (verification is meaningless if the mount pattern is wrong).
close_reason: OverlayManager now mounts lazy overlays only when open (stack-driven). Typecheck + KeyboardManager tests pass.

title: Overlay stack limit UX: handle MAX_STACK_SIZE without silent failure
description:
## Problem
When users open multiple overlays (Help → Analysis Menu → a tool overlay, etc.) we cap the overlay stack size and silently drop additional opens.

This is a trust-killer because:
- the user performs an action (“open overlay X”) and nothing happens
- there is no visible explanation (“too many overlays open”)
- it feels broken rather than intentionally constrained

### Evidence / where to look
- `packages/web/src/components/overlays/OverlayProvider.tsx` defines `MAX_STACK_SIZE = 3` (previously observed around ~L150).
- Current behavior: when stack is full, new opens are ignored (no toast, no affordance).

## Goal
If we enforce a stack cap, it must be **explicit and user-comprehensible**.

## Proposed approach (choose, implement, document)
### Option A — Feedback + prevention (minimal change)
- When stack is full, show a toast/inline notice:
  - “Close an overlay before opening another.”
  - Provide a one-click recovery action: “Close top overlay” (or “Close all”).

### Option B — Automatic replacement (recommended for intent)
- When stack is full, opening a new overlay replaces the topmost overlay.
- Still show subtle feedback (“Replaced top overlay”) so users understand what happened.

### Option C — Increase cap (only if justified)
- Raise `MAX_STACK_SIZE` (e.g., 4–5) and still add feedback when exceeded.

## Decision criteria
- Desktop keyboard-first flows typically tolerate replacement well.
- Mobile bottom sheets often *prefer* replacement (users perceive one “sheet” context).
- If we keep a hard cap, a visible recovery affordance is mandatory.

## Testing plan (must)
### E2E (Playwright)
- Add an end-to-end test that:
  - opens overlays until the cap is reached
  - attempts to open one more
  - asserts we do **not** silently fail (toast or replacement policy is observed)

### Logging requirements
- Use `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.1` harness.
- The e2e log must record:
  - the overlay ids opened (in order)
  - the observed behavior when exceeding the cap

## Acceptance criteria
- Attempting to open an overlay when at cap always produces a visible response.
- Users can recover without guessing (close top / close all / replacement).
- Keyboard behavior remains predictable:
  - Escape closes the topmost surface
  - no focus traps regress
- E2E coverage prevents the silent-failure regression.

## Notes
- If we add a toast, ensure it respects reduced motion and uses existing notification patterns (don’t invent a new one-off).
close_reason: Overlay stack cap is no longer silent: show toast w/ overlay titles + Undo (with data-testid hooks). Typecheck passes.

title: Web design system: tokens + primitives (reduce inline styles)
description:
## Problem
Web UI consistency erodes when key surfaces rely on inline styles and ad-hoc CSS. This increases:
- visual drift (spacing, typography, colors)
- maintenance cost
- subtle UI bugs (especially in overlays)

## Goal
Establish a lightweight, enforceable design system that matches Phage Explorer’s identity:
- analysis-first clarity
- premium “quiet confidence” aesthetic
- strong hierarchy, consistent overlay chrome

## Approach
- Identify high-traffic UI primitives and standardize them:
  - Overlay container/header/footer
  - Buttons, toggles, icon buttons
  - Section headings, form rows
  - Empty states, error states
- Prefer CSS variables / tokens and small reusable components.
- Incrementally replace inline styles in:
  - overlay components
  - app shell chrome

## Acceptance criteria
- Core overlay surfaces have **no new inline styles**.
- Key primitives are reused across overlays.
- Spacing and typography are consistent across major screens.

## Notes / touchpoints
- `packages/web/src/components/overlays/*`
- `packages/web/src/styles/*`
close_reason: All subtasks completed: design system tokens and primitives implemented

Common repeated inline patterns:
- info panels: padding 0.5-0.75rem, background colors.backgroundAlt, borderRadius 4-6px, textDim/muted, fontSize 0.75-0.85rem
- control rows: display flex, gap 0.5-1rem, alignItems center, flexWrap wrap
- card/list rows: border 1px colors.borderLight, background colors.backgroundAlt, borderRadius 6px
- legends: vertical stacks with 0.25rem gaps, small font, muted text

## Reduction plan
Phase 1 (foundation)
- Add overlay utility classes to `packages/web/src/styles/components.css` (avoid new file):

Phase 2 (highest impact)
- Migrate the top 5 overlays above to use utility classes.
- Replace inline typography (fontSize, color) with shared classes.
- Keep per-overlay unique layout inline only where truly custom.

Phase 3 (rest of overlays + shared components)

- Convert Model3DView inline styles into shared classes since it appears in multiple contexts.

Phase 4 (guardrail)

## Acceptance criteria

- Clear migration order is recorded.

title: Footer build metadata: remove placeholder '0.0.0' and wire real version (or hide in prod)
description:
## Problem

- Surface build metadata in:
  - Settings → About
  - or a dev-only debug panel

### Option B — Display a real build identifier
- Wire a real version/build string via Vite env injection:
  - `package.json` version at build time
  - Vercel commit SHA (`VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA`) or deployment id

Important: decide which version we mean:
- web package version (`@phage-explorer/web`), or
- root product version (`phage-explorer`)

## Testing plan (must)

- Add a simple test that asserts:
  - placeholder `0.0.0` is not rendered / not present in the build metadata helper
  - when build metadata is enabled, it is non-empty and matches expected formatting

### E2E (Playwright)

Use the logging harness from `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.1`.

## Acceptance criteria

title: Welcome/onboarding overlay: migrate to overlay primitives + premium first-run flow

## Why this matters
The Welcome/onboarding overlay is the *first impression* surface. If it feels “gamey”, inconsistent, or slightly off, users subconsciously downgrade the product’s credibility.

- secondary actions (Skip, close) are not consistently presented

Bring Welcome/onboarding up to Phase 7 standards:

- excellent keyboard and mobile behavior
- visually consistent with overlay primitives + typography + CTA system

### 2) Visual polish second

This split prevents us from mixing interaction fixes with large visual refactors and keeps regressions easier to diagnose.

## Testing expectations
- E2E coverage for the flow lives in `phage_explorer-s4qx.3.9.1`.
- Visual regression artifacts live in `phage_explorer-s4qx.3.9.2` and QA umbrella `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.7`.

## Acceptance criteria
- Welcome interaction model is obvious on first run.
- Keyboard/mobile parity is preserved.
- Final visuals match Phase 7 typography + CTA standards.
- Regression tests prevent backsliding.

  - avoid heavy repaints on mobile

## Acceptance criteria
- Default look is premium and analysis-first.
- Reduced-motion users see minimal/no animation.
- Mobile scroll remains stable; FX do not flicker.

## Touchpoints

- settings/preferences persistence

description:
## Problem

- subtle depth
- restrained accents
- clear hierarchy

- accents feel intentional (used for primary actions + selection), not ubiquitous
- surfaces have subtle elevation and borders
- text contrast is high enough for readability without relying on glow

This provides a “before/after” artifact and catches obvious regressions.

## Acceptance criteria

- Selection/primary actions remain obvious without neon outlines everywhere.
- No readability regressions in low-contrast areas.
- Visual artifacts make regressions easy to spot.

title: Button + CTA polish: consistent hierarchy (primary/secondary/ghost) across overlays and shell
description:
## Problem
Primary actions are visually strong (good), but the overall button/CTA system can feel inconsistent:
- “Skip” vs “Next” in onboarding
- icon buttons vs pills vs chips
- inconsistent padding/radius across surfaces

In premium apps, CTAs are predictable:
- primary = one obvious action
- secondary = clearly secondary
- tertiary/ghost = low emphasis

## Goal
Standardize CTA hierarchy so the UI feels cohesive and intentional.

## Proposed approach
- Define (or confirm) a small set of button variants:
  - Primary
  - Secondary
  - Ghost/tertiary
  - IconButton

- Ensure consistent:
  - radius
  - padding
  - typography
  - hover/pressed states
  - disabled states

- Apply first to the most visible surfaces:
  - Welcome/onboarding footer actions
  - overlay footers
  - top-level shell buttons (Analyze, 3D)

## Testing plan
### Unit (Bun)
- Add/extend unit tests for the button primitives to verify:
  - variant -> class/token mapping
  - disabled state styling invariants (e.g., minimum contrast)

### Visual regression
- Ensure the curated screenshot set in `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.7` captures at least:
  - Welcome footer actions
  - a representative overlay footer

## Acceptance criteria
- Every surface uses one of the standard button variants.
- Primary vs secondary actions are visually obvious.
- Disabled buttons never look “broken” or low-contrast.
- Visual artifacts help detect regressions.

## Notes
Coordinate with design-system primitives work so we don’t create new one-off components.

title: Mobile nav + FAB polish: avoid overlap, respect safe areas, and clarify primary action
description:
## Problem

## Goal
Make the mobile navigation system feel purposeful:
- primary navigation is clear
- primary action (if any) is clear
- nothing overlaps or feels accidental

## Proposed approach
- Audit bottom nav + FAB layout with safe-area insets.
- Decide the role of the FAB:
  - If it’s a primary action, it should be consistently meaningful.
  - If it’s contextual, hide it when not applicable (or show a clear tooltip / reason).
- Ensure disabled states have a reason:
  - tooltip / small label (“Select a tool to enable”)

## Testing plan (must)
### E2E (Playwright)
- Extend `packages/web/e2e/mobile-ux-audit.e2e.ts` to assert:
  - FAB does not overlap bottom nav or obscure content
  - safe-area insets are respected
  - disabled FAB state has an explanation (text or tooltip)

### Logging requirements
- Use `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.1` harness.
- Capture a screenshot artifact for at least one mobile viewport showing FAB + nav.

## Acceptance criteria
- FAB never overlaps critical UI or nav.
- Safe-area is respected on iOS/Android.
- Disabled state is understandable.
- E2E coverage prevents regressions.

## Notes
Coordinate with existing mobile bottom-sheet overlay patterns so the nav and overlays feel like one system.

- Empty states suggest next step.
- Errors provide a retry path when possible.

title: Phage selection: prevent stale async loads (request token/cancel) + surface loading/errors
description:
## Problem
Rapidly changing the selected phage can create an async race:
- user selects Phage A
- async load for A starts
- user quickly selects Phage B
- async load for A resolves after B, overwriting state and UI with stale data

User impact:
- details panel can show the wrong phage
- analysis tools may compute using stale sequence
- feels “glitchy” and erodes trust

### Evidence / where to look
- `packages/web/src/App.tsx` selection flow / `loadPhage()` (previously observed around ~L423).
- The current implementation does not appear to track an in-flight request token or abort/ignore stale results.

## Steps to Reproduce
1) Open the phage list.
2) Click/select Phage A.
3) Immediately click/select Phage B (before A finishes loading).
4) Observe the details panel or downstream surfaces can end up reflecting Phage A (stale) even though B is selected.

## Root cause
Async operations are not coupled to a “current selection request id”. There is no cancellation or stale-result guard.

## Goal
Selection changes should be deterministic:
- UI always reflects the most recently selected phage
- loading state is clear during transitions
- errors are presented in a friendly, recoverable way

## Proposed approach
1) Add stale-result protection
- Use one of:
  - an incrementing `requestId` stored in a ref/store; only apply results if `requestId` matches
  - `AbortController` if the underlying fetch supports abort

2) Tie loading state to the current request
- When selection changes, set loading state for *that* selection.
- Ensure loading state always clears (including early-return paths).

3) Surface errors
- If load fails (DB not ready, missing record, etc.), show:
  - friendly message (“Couldn’t load phage data”)
  - retry affordance
  - optional expandable details (dev-friendly)

## Testing plan (must)
### Unit/integration (Bun)
- Add a deterministic unit test that simulates two in-flight selection loads resolving out of order.
- The test must fail if the stale result can overwrite the latest selection.

### E2E (Playwright)
- Add an end-to-end test that selects two phages in quick succession and asserts the UI reflects the latest selection.
- If production timing is too fast, introduce a *test-only delay hook* guarded behind a Playwright-only flag.

### Logging requirements
- Unit tests: include request ids + resolution order in assertion failure messages.
- E2E: use `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.1` harness and record selection events.

## Acceptance criteria
- Selecting phages rapidly never results in stale data displayed.
- The final selected phage always matches the details panel and dependent surfaces.
- Loading indicator is visible during transitions and always clears.
- Failures are actionable (retry) and do not require full refresh.
- Unit + e2e coverage prevents regressions.

## Notes
This is a correctness fix, not just polish. It directly supports Phase 7 goals of trustworthiness and perceived performance.

## Related
QA umbrella: `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.5`.
close_reason: Added request token pattern to loadPhage() - guards against stale async results when rapidly switching phages

title: DB initialization UX: progress, retry, offline clarity
description:

title: Header DB status: replace dev-speak ('db: ready') with user-facing status + debug-only details
description:
## Problem
The app header currently exposes DB state with developer-oriented labels like:
- `db: ready`
- `cached`
- `loading`

This reads like internal debug UI and makes the product feel unfinished/untrustworthy.

### Evidence / where to look
- `packages/web/src/App.tsx` header status rendering (previously observed around ~L712).

## Goal
Provide a premium, user-facing status model:
- by default, hide internal implementation details
- when the DB is unavailable or loading, communicate clearly and provide recovery
- optionally allow a debug mode to show precise internal states (for developers)

## Proposed approach
### Default (prod UX)
- Show nothing when DB is healthy.
- When DB is loading/unavailable, show a subtle status chip:
  - “Loading database…”
  - “Database unavailable — Retry”

### Debug mode (dev UX)
- A dev-only flag or Settings toggle that reveals implementation detail:
  - “db: cached” / “asset fetch failed” etc.

## Testing plan (must)
### E2E (Playwright)
- Add an assertion that on a healthy load:
  - no `db:` dev-speak is visible in the header
- Add an assertion for the failure/retry path (as feasible):
  - a user-facing message appears
  - retry button is present and works

Use the logging harness from `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.1`:
- capture console/page errors
- record DB status transitions in `events.jsonl`

## Acceptance criteria
- Normal users never see “db: ready/cached” style copy.
- When DB load is slow or fails, users get clear, actionable UI (retry).
- Developers can still see detailed status when they opt in.
- E2E coverage prevents regressions.

## Notes
This complements DB init work in `phage_explorer-s4qx.6.3` and error boundary work in `phage_explorer-s4qx.6.6`.
close_reason: Replaced dev-speak (db: ready/loading/etc) with user-friendly messaging (Loading... or nothing when ready)

title: 3D viewer controls: style Quality selector (no white native dropdown in dark UI)
description:
## Problem
In the 3D Structure panel, the Quality selector currently presents as an unstyled native dropdown (white menu) inside the dark UI.

- can be hard to read (low contrast) depending on OS styles

## Goal
All interactive controls inside the 3D viewer panel should feel native to the app:
- consistent dark theme styling
- consistent spacing, typography, and focus ring

- Fallback: apply robust cross-browser styling to the existing select + options.

If we introduce or reuse a dropdown primitive, it should be reused for other selects (Settings, analysis option pickers) to reduce one-off styling.

## Testing plan (must)
### E2E (Playwright)

title: 3D default + copy alignment: decide default (mobile/desktop) and ensure UI never lies
description:
## Problem
The UI copy around 3D appears inconsistent with actual defaults.

Example (as previously observed):
- `packages/web/src/App.tsx` includes copy implying 3D is “Disabled by default” (around ~L1120)
- but the Zustand default is `show3DModel: true` in `packages/state/src/store.ts` (around ~L302)

Even if the behavior is acceptable, *lying copy* is worse than a suboptimal default.

## Goal
Make 3D behavior and copy coherent:
- decide and document the actual default policy (desktop vs mobile)
- encode defaults in one place
- ensure UI copy and settings reflect reality

## Proposed approach
1) Decide default policy (document the choice)
- Option A: Enable 3D by default on desktop, disable on mobile / low-power devices.
- Option B: Disable by default everywhere, user enables intentionally.
- Option C: Enable everywhere, but only when structure is available and device is capable.

Decision inputs to consider:
- mobile CPU/GPU constraints
- perceived jank vs value
- how often structures are available
- whether “3D on” is more like a feature toggle or core mode

2) Encode defaults in one place
- Ensure there is one canonical source of default truth (state initialization).
- Avoid duplicating default assumptions in UI copy.

3) Align copy + settings
- Any “disabled by default” copy must be generated from the same source.
- If defaults vary by device, copy must say so.

## Testing plan (must)
### Unit (Bun)
- Add a unit test that asserts:
  - the default `show3DModel` policy is exactly what we decided (including any device-gated logic)
  - any helper that generates 3D copy cannot disagree with the default

### E2E (Playwright)
- Add an assertion that:
  - the visible 3D copy matches the actual effective default on that device profile
  - toggling 3D via UI updates state and persists

Use the structured logging harness from `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.1`.

## Acceptance criteria
- The default 3D state is clearly defined and implemented.
- UI copy about 3D defaults is always accurate.
- Settings toggle reflects real current state and persists correctly.
- No confusing “Available” status vs actual panel visibility mismatch.
- Unit + e2e tests prevent future mismatch.

## Related
- `phage_explorer-s4qx.5.2` (FX/defaults consolidation) is related because 3D defaults often interact with perceived FX intensity.
- QA umbrella: `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.7` (visual artifacts) for any copy/UX drift.
close_reason: Fully implemented: device-aware defaults, aligned UI copy, unit + E2E tests all in place

title: Keyboard + focus conventions (no conflicts, predictable Escape)
description:
## Problem
Keyboard-first UX is a core feature. Ad-hoc key listeners and inconsistent focus handling can cause:
- shortcuts firing while typing in inputs
- inconsistent Escape-to-close behavior
- conflicts between overlays/menus

## Goal
Create a single, predictable model for:
- global shortcuts (layer 0/1)
- context shortcuts (only when overlay/menu is open)
- focus rules (inputs disable global shortcuts except explicit)
- Escape behavior (close topmost overlay/menu)

## Approach
- Document conventions (in-code and/or README)
- Audit `window.addEventListener('keydown')` usage and replace with shared mechanisms
- Ensure consistent behavior across overlays, bottom sheets, command palette

## Acceptance criteria
- No global shortcuts fire while typing, unless intentionally allowed.
- Escape always closes the topmost surface.
- Hotkey definitions flow through the same registry/path.

## Touchpoints
- `useHotkey`
- OverlayProvider/manager
- command palette / search inputs
close_reason: All children complete: focus rules defined, ad-hoc listeners audited, Escape behavior consistent, search/command palette UX solid, surface hints implemented, regression tests in place

title: Platform hotkeys: add Cmd/Ctrl+K (palette) and Cmd/Ctrl+, (settings) as first-class bindings
description:
## Problem
Phage Explorer is keyboard-first, but some keybindings do not follow widely learned platform conventions:
- Command palette is commonly `Cmd+K` (mac) / `Ctrl+K` (win/linux)
- Settings is commonly `Cmd+,` (mac) / `Ctrl+,` (win/linux)

Today, the registry/UX appears to be inconsistent:
- Some UI hints mention `Cmd+K`, but ActionRegistry binds command palette to `:`.
- Settings appears bound only to `Ctrl+,`, which is not discoverable for mac users.

This causes avoidable friction because users bring muscle memory from Stripe/Linear/Figma/etc.

### References
- Command palette action: `packages/web/src/keyboard/actionRegistry.ts` (previously observed around ~L224).
- Settings action: `packages/web/src/keyboard/actionRegistry.ts` (previously observed around ~L238).

## Goal
Adopt platform-standard shortcuts as **first-class** bindings while:
- avoiding conflicts
- preserving the keyboard-first identity
- ensuring we never trigger shortcuts while typing in inputs

## Proposed approach
1) Decide canonical shortcuts
- Command palette: primary `Cmd/Ctrl+K`
- Settings: primary `Cmd/Ctrl+,`

2) Preserve existing bindings as optional aliases (if we choose)
- Keep `:` for command palette as an alternate (useful for vim/tui-style users), but ensure it:
  - does not trigger while typing in inputs
  - does not conflict with other layer-0 keys

3) Represent multi-shortcut actions in ActionRegistry
- Support:
  - per-platform primary shortcut
  - alternates
  - consistent formatting for display surfaces

4) Validate conflicts and focus rules
- Update conflict detection to treat multi-shortcut actions correctly.
- Ensure focus rules remain strict (no global shortcuts while typing).

## Testing plan (must)
### Unit (Bun)
- Extend keyboard conflict tests to assert:
  - Cmd/Ctrl+K and Cmd/Ctrl+, do not conflict with existing global shortcuts
  - `:` (if kept) is still registered but scope-limited
- Extend focus-rule tests (if present) to ensure shortcuts do not fire while an input/textarea is focused.

Suggested touchpoints:
- `packages/web/src/keyboard/validateConflicts.test.ts`
- `packages/web/src/keyboard/KeyboardManager.test.ts`

### E2E (Playwright)
- Add/extend tests to assert:
  - `Meta+K` / `Control+K` opens command palette
  - `Meta+,` / `Control+,` opens settings
  - `:` still works (if kept)
  - none of these fire while typing in an input

Use the logging harness from `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.1`.

## Acceptance criteria
- On macOS: `Cmd+K` opens the command palette; `Cmd+,` opens Settings.
- On win/linux: `Ctrl+K` opens the command palette; `Ctrl+,` opens Settings.
- Existing `:` binding (if kept) still works, but never fires while typing.
- Shortcut hints and command palette display update automatically (because `phage_explorer-s4qx.1.7.3` removed hardcoded hint strings).
- Unit + e2e coverage prevents regressions.

## Dependencies
This task is intentionally blocked by:
- `phage_explorer-s4qx.1.7.3` (we must remove hardcoded hint strings before we change canonical shortcuts)

## Related
QA umbrella: `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.3` (e2e) and `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.6` (unit).

title: Phase 7 QA automation: unit + e2e regression suite (with structured logs)
description:
## Why this exists
Phase 7 is largely about *trust and polish*:
- shortcuts always do what they say
- overlays feel intentional, not fragile
- loading/error states are clear and recoverable
- mobile interactions feel native

These are exactly the kinds of improvements that tend to regress unless we lock them in with automated tests.

## High-level goal
Create a regression safety net that is:
- **Comprehensive** for Phase 7 critical paths
- **Deterministic** (stable selectors, minimal flake)
- **High-signal** (failures are actionable, not noisy)
- **Well-instrumented** (logs + artifacts explain what happened)

## Scope
### Unit/integration (Bun)
- Validate ActionRegistry-driven UI surfaces cannot drift:
  - command palette
  - app-shell shortcut hints
  - analysis sidebar tool list + shortcut badges
  - mobile ActionDrawer items
- Validate keyboard conflict detection for multi-shortcut actions.
- Validate selection/load race guards (stale request protection).

### E2E (Playwright)
Leverage the existing Playwright suite in `packages/web/e2e/` to add Phase 7 coverage with strong logging:
- overlay lazy-load chunking (no overlay chunk requests on cold load)
- platform-standard shortcuts (Cmd/Ctrl+K, Cmd/Ctrl+, plus any supported aliases like `:`)
- overlay stack behavior (cap behavior is explicit and recoverable)
- phage selection race determinism (latest selection always wins)
- 3D panel UX (quality dropdown themed; copy matches defaults)
- mobile safe-area / FAB / bottom-nav overlap and scroll stability

## Observability requirements (critical)
E2E tests must capture and persist:
- page errors and console errors
- key network requests (especially dynamic chunks)
- screenshots/traces/videos on failure (already enabled; ensure attachments are meaningful)

Prefer structured artifacts written to `testInfo.outputPath(...)`:
- `events.jsonl` (timestamped steps/events)
- `console-errors.json`
- `network-chunks.json`

## Success criteria
- Every Phase 7 bead that changes user-facing behavior has:
  - at least 1 targeted unit/integration test where feasible, and
  - at least 1 targeted e2e assertion in Playwright for user-visible flows.
- When a test fails, logs clearly explain:
  - what action was attempted
  - what was observed

title: Playwright logging harness: structured events + console/network capture
description:
## Problem
We already have many Playwright tests under `packages/web/e2e/`, but logging/diagnostics patterns vary by file. When failures happen, it’s often unclear:
- what the test was trying to do
- what the app did instead
- which console/network errors occurred

## Goal
Standardize Playwright observability so failures are fast to debug and high-signal.

## Proposed approach
Create a small shared helper (keep file sprawl minimal) used by all Phase 7-related e2e tests:

### Required capture
- `page.on('pageerror', ...)` with stack/message capture
- `page.on('console', ...)` capturing at least:
  - errors
  - warnings (optional, but useful for deprecations)
- `page.on('request')` / `page.on('response')` capture for:
  - dynamic chunk requests
  - DB asset requests (phage.db, wasm, workers)

### Structured artifacts (write per-test)
Persist artifacts under `testInfo.outputPath(...)` so they appear next to traces/videos:
- `events.jsonl`: timestamped events and `test.step` boundaries
- `console-errors.json`: array of console error entries
- `page-errors.json`: array of uncaught errors
- `network.json`: filtered requests/responses (URL, status, timing)

### Reporting conventions
- Use `test.step('...', async () => { ... })` for major steps.
- When asserting, include the most useful context in error messages (expected vs actual).

## Acceptance criteria
- A single helper can be imported by Phase 7 e2e files and produces consistent artifacts.
- At least these existing suites are migrated to use it:
  - `packages/web/e2e/repro.e2e.ts`
  - `packages/web/e2e/database.e2e.ts`
  - `packages/web/e2e/production-health.e2e.ts`
  - `packages/web/e2e/mobile-ux-audit.e2e.ts`
- On failure, the artifacts make root-cause obvious without re-running locally.

## Notes
- Keep logging *test-side* (do not introduce noisy `console.log` in UI components).
- Coordinate with `phage_explorer-s4qx.6.6` so error boundaries still surface meaningful messages without telemetry.
close_reason: Implemented Playwright logging harness (test-harness.ts) with structured artifact capture. Migrated repro.e2e.ts, database.e2e.ts, production-health.e2e.ts, and mobile-ux-audit.e2e.ts to use the harness.

title: E2E stability: add data-testid hooks for critical Phase 7 surfaces

## Problem
Many current Playwright tests rely on brittle selectors (classnames, text, broad role queries). As Phase 7 polish refactors UI structure and styling, tests will flake or become expensive to maintain.

## Goal
Introduce a minimal, intentional set of `data-testid` hooks so tests are:
- stable across styling refactors
- readable (tests communicate intent)
- easy to debug (selectors map to product concepts)

## Proposed approach

### 3D panel
- quality dropdown trigger and menu
- 3D availability status chip

### DB status

## Acceptance criteria
- Phase 7 e2e tests stop relying on classnames for critical paths.
- Selectors are documented (short comment in test helper or a short doc section).

## Notes

title: E2E regression: overlay lazy-load chunking (no eager overlay chunks on cold start)
description:
## Problem
Overlay chunking regressions are easy to introduce accidentally (e.g., by mounting all `React.lazy` overlays on cold start). These regressions are hard to catch without explicitly inspecting the Network panel.

## Goal
Make overlay chunking correctness *automatic* via Playwright assertions + logs.

## Coverage
- On cold load (no overlays opened):
  - no overlay chunks are fetched
  - no overlay code is evaluated due to eager mounting

- After opening a specific overlay (e.g., Help):
  - that overlay’s chunk is fetched
  - unrelated overlays remain unfetched

## Logging requirements
- Persist a filtered `network-chunks.json` artifact listing any request that matches:
  - `/assets/.*\.js` chunk URLs
  - overlay chunk name patterns (document what patterns we use)

## Suggested implementation approach
- Add a focused Playwright test that:
  - hooks network listeners early
  - visits `/` and waits for app idle
  - asserts *no* overlay chunk URLs were requested
  - opens one overlay via keyboard
  - asserts that overlay chunk URL(s) were requested after the open

Prefer extending `packages/web/e2e/production-health.e2e.ts` or adding a small dedicated file if that’s cleaner.

## Acceptance criteria
- Fails loudly if overlay chunks are fetched before any overlay is opened.
- Produces actionable output: list of unexpected chunk URLs and the timing/order they were requested.

## Dependencies
This task should be executed alongside:
- `phage_explorer-s4qx.2.6` (only mount overlays when open)
- `phage_explorer-s4qx.2.4` (manual verification notes)
close_reason: Enhanced overlay-lazy-loading.e2e.ts: comprehensive chunk detection, network-chunks.json artifact, verifies no eager loads on cold start, chunk loaded on demand after opening overlay, cross-overlay isolation test

title: Regression: phage selection determinism (stale-load guard) with unit + e2e tests
description:
## Problem
The “stale async load overwrites the latest selection” bug is subtle and often only appears under timing pressure.

If we fix it without tests, it will likely regress during future refactors.

## Goal
Make selection determinism a permanent invariant:
- last selection always wins
- stale results are ignored
- loading/errors are user-friendly

## Unit/integration test plan (Bun)
- Extract the selection/load sequencing into a testable function or store action.
- Add a unit test that simulates:
  - request A starts
  - request B starts
  - request A resolves last
  - ensure state reflects B and A is ignored

The unit test must log (in assertion failure messages):
- request ids
- resolution order
- which result applied

## E2E test plan (Playwright)
- Extend `packages/web/e2e/database.e2e.ts` (or similar) to:
  - select a phage
  - immediately select another phage
  - assert the UI reflects the *second* phage

### Determinism strategy
If the production UI is too fast to reliably reproduce, add a **test-only delay hook** that is:
- disabled in production builds
- enabled only when Playwright sets a known flag (e.g., query param or `window.__E2E__`)

This must be designed carefully to avoid shipping “test behavior” to users.

## Logging requirements
Use the harness from `phage_explorer-s4qx.8.1` and additionally record:
- selected phage IDs/names in `events.jsonl`
- any load errors

## Acceptance criteria
- Unit test fails if stale results can overwrite current selection.
- E2E test fails if UI ever shows stale selection data.
- Logs make the failure cause obvious.

## Related
- `phage_explorer-s4qx.6.2.1` (fix)

title: [WEB] Phage Explorer Web Application Deployment
description:
# Master Epic: Phage Explorer Web Application Deployment

## Vision
Transform Phage Explorer from a terminal application into a browser-native experience that *amplifies* the cyberpunk aesthetic through GPU-accelerated visuals, while preserving—and enhancing—the keyboard-driven immediacy that makes the TUI feel alive.

## Strategic Goals
1. **Preserve** the keyboard-first, low-latency interaction model
2. **Amplify** the cyberpunk aesthetic with GPU-accelerated effects (phosphor glow, scanlines, chromatic aberration)
3. **Extend** capabilities with web-only features (collaboration, video export, offline)
4. **Maintain** a single codebase for core logic and computation via shared packages
5. **Deploy** seamlessly on Vercel with no backend infrastructure

## Technical Approach
- **Framework**: React 19 + Vite + Bun
- **State**: Zustand (shared with TUI)
- **Rendering**: Canvas 2D + WebGL for effects + WebGPU (experimental)
- **Database**: sql.js (SQLite WASM) with IndexedDB caching
- **Offline**: Service Worker with Workbox
- **Deployment**: Vercel static hosting + edge functions

## Architecture Overview
```
packages/
├── core/              # Shared (existing)
├── state/             # Shared (existing) + web persistence layer
├── wasm-compute/      # Shared (existing)
├── db-runtime/        # Extended with browser adapter
├── web/               # NEW: Web application
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── app/       # React app structure
│   │   ├── components/
│   │   ├── rendering/ # Canvas/WebGL renderers
│   │   ├── workers/   # Web Workers
│   │   └── service-worker/
└── tui/               # Existing (preserved)
```

## Design Principles
1. **Terminal Authenticity, Not Simulation** - We adopt the aesthetic vocabulary (monospace, scanlines, phosphor glow) while exploiting web's superpowers
2. **Keyboard-First, Mouse-Aware** - Every action is keyboard-accessible, mouse/touch are accelerators
3. **Instant Feedback** - <16ms visual feedback, <50ms action completion, <150ms complex computations
4. **Progressive Disclosure** - Novice→Intermediate→Power user journey
5. **Offline-First** - Complete functionality after first load

## Success Metrics
- First Contentful Paint: <1.0s
- Time to Interactive: <2.0s
- Keypress to Paint: <16ms
- 60fps scrolling on 100k+ base sequences
- 100% hotkey parity with TUI
- 100% overlay parity with TUI
- Full offline functionality

## Phased Execution
- **Phase 0**: Foundation (scaffold, themes, keyboard)
- **Phase 1**: Data Layer (sql.js, caching, offline)
- **Phase 2**: Core Visualization (canvas sequence grid, gene map, sparklines)
- **Phase 3**: Overlays & Panels (command palette, analysis menu, overlays)
- **Phase 4**: Simulations (worker orchestration, all sims)
- **Phase 5**: Advanced Features (heavy analysis, WebGPU, collaboration)
- **Phase 6**: Polish & Launch (performance, accessibility, onboarding)

## References
- See PLAN_TO_DEPLOY_PHAGE_EXPLORER_AS_WEBAPP.md for full technical specifications

title: [WEB-P4] Simulations: Worker-Based Computation Engine
description:
# Phase 4: Simulations (Target: Weeks 7-9)

## Purpose
Port all simulation capabilities to the web, running in Web Workers to avoid blocking the UI thread.

## Why This Matters
Simulations are what make Phage Explorer educational and research-useful. They transform static sequence data into dynamic, explorable processes. Without them, the web version is significantly less valuable than the TUI.

## Technical Strategy
All heavy computation runs in Web Workers:
1. **Main Thread**: UI, user input, rendering coordination
2. **Workers**: Simulation logic, WASM execution, analysis

We use **Comlink** for type-safe worker communication, avoiding raw postMessage complexity.

## Deliverables
1. **Worker Orchestration** - ComputeOrchestrator class
2. **Ribosome Traffic Simulation** - Polysome dynamics
3. **Lysogeny Circuit Simulation** - CI/Cro decision circuit
4. **Plaque Automata** - Cellular automaton plaque growth
5. **Evolution Replay** - Temporal mutation replay
6. **Time Controls** - Unified playback UI

## Worker Architecture
```typescript
class ComputeOrchestrator {
  workers: Map<string, Worker>  // 'analysis', 'simulation', 'wasm'
  
  async runAnalysis<T>(type, data, options): Promise<T>
  runWithProgress<T>(type, data, onProgress): Promise<T>
}
```

### Worker Pool
| Worker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| analysis | GC skew, complexity, k-mer analysis |
| simulation | Ribosome, lysogeny, evolution |
| wasm | WASM kernel execution |

## Simulation Specifications

### Ribosome Traffic
- Models polysome collisions and stalling
- Codon-by-codon translation timing
- Visualizes ribosome density along mRNA

### Lysogeny Circuit
- CI/Cro regulatory dynamics
- Stochastic gene expression
- Predicts lysis vs lysogeny decision

### Plaque Automata
- Cellular automaton grid
- Phage diffusion model
- Visual plaque growth over time

### Evolution Replay
- Temporal sequence changes
- Ancestral state reconstruction
- Phylogenetic context

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Simulations run without blocking UI (no frame drops)
- [ ] Progress indicators work for long computations
- [ ] Snapshots can be saved and restored
- [ ] Deterministic with seed (reproducible)
- [ ] Time controls work consistently across sims
- [ ] Cancel button stops running simulations

## Performance Targets
| Operation | Target |
|-----------|--------|
| UI frame time during sim | <16ms |
| Simulation step | <100ms |
| Full ribosome sim (50kb) | <10s |

## Risks & Mitigations
- **Risk**: Worker communication overhead
  - **Mitigation**: Batch updates, use SharedArrayBuffer if supported
- **Risk**: Memory pressure from long simulations
  - **Mitigation**: Chunked processing, dispose old results
- **Risk**: Different timing across browsers
  - **Mitigation**: Use performance.now(), not Date.now()

## Dependencies
- Phase 2 (visualization for simulation output)
- Phase 3 (simulation hub modal)
- Existing simulation code in TUI packages

## Findings

Two ad-hoc scripts sit at the repository root, outside `scripts/`:

- `test-core.ts` — "Test script to verify core functionality works", importing
  `BunSqliteRepository` directly from `./packages/db-runtime/src`. It is not part of

  any script in `package.json`.
- `debug-console.mjs` — a Playwright script that launches chromium at 1400x900, evidently
  used once to capture console output during debugging.

## Why this is worth a bead at all

AGENTS.md sets a deliberately high bar for files ("New files are only for genuinely new
domains that don't fit existing modules. The bar for adding files is very high") and
forbids parallel testing arrangements. Two untracked-by-any-script test and debug entry
points at the root are exactly the sprawl that rule exists to prevent, and a future agent
may reasonably mistake `test-core.ts` for part of the test suite.

## The action

For each: fold it into the proper place (a real test under the relevant package; a
documented script under `scripts/`), or seek approval to remove it.

Per AGENTS.md RULE 1, removal requires explicit written approval in-session before any
deletion command is proposed. State the exact files and wait.

## Acceptance criteria

- Neither file remains at the root without a documented purpose.
- If removed, the approving instruction and command are recorded here.

Advanced: Structural Epitope Clash Map
description:
## Structural Epitope Clash Map (Tail Fiber Host Range Analyzer)

### Concept
The tail fiber is the phage's MOLECULAR KEY — its receptor-binding domain (RBD) determines host specificity. This feature combines:
1. **Structural analysis**: ΔΔG alanine scans and electrostatics on predicted structures
2. **Modular domain detection**: Identify N-anchor, shaft, and hypervariable RBD regions
3. **Entropy-based variability mapping**: Find conserved vs rapidly-evolving positions
4. **Host range prediction**: Infer likely hosts from RBD sequence features

### Mathematical Foundations

**Shannon entropy for per-position variability:**
H(i) = -Σ p(a) × log₂(p(a)) for each alignment position
- H(i) = 0: Perfectly conserved (functional constraint)
- H(i) = 4.3: Maximum entropy (20 AA, no constraint)
Entropy profile reveals low entropy in anchor/shaft (structural), high in RBD (host-range variability)

**Domain boundary detection:**
Tail fibers have conserved modular structure: [N-anchor] — [Shaft repeats] — [RBD]
Detect via:
- Entropy gradient peaks (sudden variability change)
- Hydropathy profile transitions
- Secondary structure predictions (α-helix shaft → β-sheet RBD)
- Recombination breakpoint detection

**Structural stability (ΔΔG):**
ΔΔG = ΔG(wild-type) - ΔG(alanine mutant)
- High ΔΔG = structurally important (core)
- Low ΔΔG = surface-exposed, tolerant to mutation
- Negative ΔΔG = destabilizing, likely under selection

**Host range prediction features:**
For ML model: k-mer frequencies (k=3,4,5), AA composition, predicted secondary structure, isoelectric point, molecular weight, specific motifs (carbohydrate-binding, Ig-like folds)

### Implementation
- entropyProfile(alignment) → Float64Array of per-position entropy
- detectDomainBoundaries(entropy, hydropathy, secondaryStructure) → DomainBoundary[]
- predictHostRange(rbdSequence, knownRBDs) → HostPrediction[] with confidence
- analyzeStructuralEpitopes(pdbId, sequence) → StructuralRisk[] (ΔΔG, surface area, charge)

### TUI Visualization (Multi-Layer)
- Domain structure bar: N-anchor | Shaft | RBD with conservation coloring
- Entropy profile sparkline (low in anchor, high in RBD)
- Structural risk profile (ΔΔG instability)
- Host range prediction table with confidence bars
- Chimera suggestion: "Swap RBD (aa 850-1132) with P22 gpJ → Predicted new host: Salmonella"
- 3D ASCII model with epitope highlighting (charge/risk mode toggle)

### Pedagogical Value: 9/10
Teaches receptor-ligand biology, protein modularity, information theory (Shannon entropy), structural biology (surface exposure, electrostatics), evolution of specificity (arms race in molecular detail).

### External Dependencies
- AlphaFold DB or ESMFold for structure prediction
- FoldX (or ML surrogate) for ΔΔG calculations
- APBS for electrostatics

### Priority: P4 (highest complexity)

description:
# Problem
Several UI components still construct workers with `{ type: "module" }` only. On some browsers (notably older Safari / partial implementations), `new Worker(url, { type: "module" })` can throw, breaking overlays (search, CRISPR, comparison, etc.).

We already have robust module→classic fallback patterns in a few places (`DatabaseLoader`, `ComputeOrchestrator`, `WorkerPreloader`, `PhagePickerSheet`), but coverage is incomplete.

# Goal
Make worker construction resilient across browsers via progressive enhancement:
- Try module worker first
- Fall back to classic worker if module worker construction throws

# Scope
Audit and patch remaining call sites, including (but not limited to):
- `packages/web/src/components/overlays/SearchOverlay.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/components/overlays/CommandPalette.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/components/overlays/ComparisonOverlay.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/components/overlays/CRISPROverlay.tsx`
- Any other overlay that directly instantiates a worker

# Constraints
- No UA sniffing; runtime try/catch fallback only.
- Avoid large refactors; keep changes localized and consistent.

# Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All direct `new Worker(..., { type: "module" })` call sites in `packages/web/src/components/overlays/**` have a module→classic fallback.
- [ ] `packages/web` build passes.
- [ ] No behavioral change on modern browsers (module workers still used when available).
notes:
Progress:
- Added module→classic Worker constructor fallback (try `{ type: "module" }`, fall back to `new Worker(url)`) for all overlay workers that were module-only: SearchOverlay, CommandPalette, CRISPROverlay, ComparisonOverlay, DotPlotOverlay, SyntenyOverlay, HilbertOverlay, CGROverlay, AnomalyOverlay.
- Made SearchOverlay worker init logs dev-only.
- UBS: eliminated critical findings by replacing loose `!= null` UI guards with strict null/undefined checks and removing `new Function()` from browser-capabilities worker detection.
- Verified `cd packages/web && bun run build` succeeds.
close_reason: Implemented module→classic fallback for all overlay workers; web build passes; UBS critical=0

title: install.sh --with-database aborts: `local` used outside a function
description:
## Severity

This breaks the exact command the README puts at the top of the page as the recommended
install:

```
curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Dicklesworthstone/phage_explorer/main/install.sh?$(date +%s)" | bash -s -- --with-database
```

## The defect

`install.sh:410` declares:

```
local decompressed_db
```

The enclosing function `install_db_from_source` ends at line 394. Line 410 sits inside the
top-level `if [[ $WITH_DATABASE -eq 1 ]]` block (starting line 396), which is not a
function body.

Bash rejects `local` outside a function ("local: can only be used in a function") with a
non-zero status. The script runs under `set -euo pipefail` (line 26), so the shell exits
immediately.

## When it fires

The failing branch is the *primary* one for a prebuilt install: it runs when the compressed
release asset `phage.db.gz` downloads successfully and `gunzip` is available — i.e. the
common case on Linux and macOS. The uncompressed fallback path below it does not use
`local` and would work.

Because the failure is an abort rather than a handled error, the user gets a bare bash
diagnostic and no installed database, after the binary has already been placed.

## Why it has gone unnoticed

No release has shipped since 2025-12-16 (see the sibling release beads), and the v1.4.1
release predates this code path, so `phage.db.gz` does not exist as a release asset. The
`curl` for it fails, the script takes the uncompressed fallback, and the bug never
executes. It will fire the moment a release publishes a `.gz` asset — i.e. immediately
after the release jam is fixed.

## The fix

- Remove the `local` keyword (the variable is fine as a plain assignment at top level), or
  move the block into a function.
- Then test all three installer paths on a clean machine: `--with-database` with a `.gz`
  asset present, `--with-database` with only the plain `.db`, and `--from-source`.
- Add a shell lint step (`shellcheck`) to CI; this class of error is exactly what it
  catches, and `install.sh` is 18 KB of untested shell that every new user runs.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `--with-database` install against a release containing `phage.db.gz` succeeds.
- `shellcheck` runs on `install.sh` in CI and passes.
close_reason: Fixed at c2b3ed4. Removed 'local' used outside a function body, which bash rejects with non-zero status and set -euo pipefail turns into an abort. Verified end to end, not by inspection: extracted the database-install block from the shipped install.sh, pointed the release URLs at a local server serving the real 3.9 MB phage.db.gz, and ran it under the same set -euo pipefail context. Before: 'local: can only be used in a function', nothing installed but a stray 3.8 MB tmp file. After: valid 10 MB SQLite database with 24 phages and 4,836 genes. Also swept for other 'local' uses outside functions; none remain.

title: Advanced: Capsid Packaging & Ejection Energetics Simulator
description: Quantify physics of packing dsDNA into capsid and ejection: force-extension, internal pressure (up to ~60 atm), salt/GC effects. Worm-Like Chain elasticity + Debye-Hückel electrostatics + bending energy. Compare headful vs cos vs phi29 portal strategies. Interactive sliders for ionic strength, temperature; fill fraction animation. Bridges genome composition to biophysical feasibility. Novelty: High, Pedagogical: High.
notes:
## CAPSID PACKAGING & EJECTION ENERGETICS SIMULATOR

**Full Implementation from Roadmap**

### Mathematical Foundations

**Worm-Like Chain (WLC) Model:**
```
F(x) = (k_B T / L_p) × [1/(4(1-x/L)²) - 1/4 + x/L]

Where:
- L_p = persistence length (~50 nm for dsDNA)
- L = contour length of DNA
- x = end-to-end extension
- k_B × T ≈ 4.1 pN·nm at 25°C
```

**Confinement Free Energy (Odijk regime):**
```
ΔG_confinement = (k_B T × L) / (L_p^(1/3) × D^(2/3))
```

**Electrostatic Repulsion (Debye-Hückel):**
```
U_elec(r) = (q² / 4πε₀ε_r) × (e^(-κr) / r)
κ = √(2 × N_A × e² × I / (ε₀ε_r k_B T))
```

**Internal Pressure:**
```
P = -(∂G/∂V) = (k_B T / V) × [N_segments + B₂ × N² / V + ...]
```

### Complete TypeScript Implementation

- `PackagingEnergetics` interface with bending, confinement, electrostatic components
- `CapsidGeometry` models: T4, Lambda, T7, Phi29, PhiX174
- `MotorProperties` for different packaging systems
- `calculateDebyeLength()`, `wlcForce()`, `calculateBendingEnergy()`
- `calculateConfinementEntropy()`, `calculateElectrostaticEnergy()`
- `calculateInternalPressure()`, `generateForceExtensionCurve()`
- `simulateEjection()` with osmotic pressure opposition
- `comparePackagingEnergetics()` for multi-phage comparison

### Implementation Stack
- **Physics Engine**: Rust + nalgebra + ndarray → WASM
- **Caching**: SQLite stores precomputed force-extension curves
- **UI**: Ink/React with Braille block plotting for smooth curves
- **Animation**: requestAnimationFrame-like loop for ejection dynamics

### TUI Features
- Force vs Fill Fraction plot with motor stall line
- Energy component breakdown (bending, confinement, electrostatic)
- Capsid fill visualization with pressure gauge
- Ejection dynamics timeline with velocity decay
- Interactive sliders: [I]onic strength, [T]emperature, [S]trategy

Novelty: 10/10, Pedagogical: 9/10, Wow Factor: 9/10

title: [WEB-P3] Add keyboard navigation (↑↓ Enter Tab Esc)
Add swipe navigation indicator arrows on mobile
description:
## Problem

The app supports horizontal swipe gestures to navigate between phages, but there's NO visual indication this is possible. Mobile users have no way to discover this feature unless told.

## Current State

- Swipe handling exists in `App.tsx:440-519` - works but invisible
- `mobile-ux.css` has `.gesture-hint` class defined but unused
- ControlDeck has Prev/Next buttons but swipe is faster for browsing

## Solution: Edge Swipe Indicators

Create persistent but subtle arrow indicators on left/right edges that:
1. Show when on mobile AND when there are phages to navigate to
2. Pulse/glow gently to attract attention (once per session)
3. Fade during/after swipe gesture (visual feedback)
4. Are positioned to avoid FAB and ControlDeck

## Visual Design

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│           PHAGE NAME                │
│                                     │
│  ◀        [main content]         ▶  │  <- Indicators at vertical center
│                                     │
│                                     │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │        ControlDeck          │    │
└──┴─────────────────────────────┴────┘
```

- **Position**: Vertical center of viewport, just outside content padding
- **Style**: Semi-transparent arrows with subtle animation
- **Z-index**: `var(--z-sticky)` (200) - below FAB/ControlDeck (300), above content
- **Visibility**: 
  - Left arrow hidden when at first phage (isFirst)
  - Right arrow hidden when at last phage (isLast)

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Create SwipeIndicators component

```tsx
// packages/web/src/components/mobile/SwipeIndicators.tsx
interface SwipeIndicatorsProps {
  isFirst: boolean;  // Hide left arrow
  isLast: boolean;   // Hide right arrow
  isVisible: boolean; // Master show/hide
  showPulse?: boolean; // Animate for new users
}
```

### 2. Add CSS with proper z-index

```css
/* packages/web/src/styles/swipe-indicators.css */
.swipe-indicator {
  position: fixed;
  top: 50%;
  transform: translateY(-50%);
  z-index: var(--z-sticky); /* 200 - below FAB/ControlDeck (300), above content */
  opacity: 0.6;
  pointer-events: none; /* Decorative only */
  transition: opacity var(--duration-normal);
}
.swipe-indicator--left { left: 8px; }
.swipe-indicator--right { right: 8px; }
.swipe-indicator--pulse { animation: swipe-hint-pulse 2s ease-in-out 3; }
.swipe-indicator--subtle { opacity: 0.3; } /* For learned users */

@keyframes swipe-hint-pulse {
  0%, 100% { opacity: 0.6; transform: translateY(-50%) scale(1); }
  50% { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(-50%) scale(1.1); }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .swipe-indicator--pulse { animation: none; }
}
```

### 3. Integrate in App.tsx

- Add SwipeIndicators to mobile render
- Pass isFirst/isLast from phage navigation state
- Show only when isMobile && phages.length > 1

## Files to Create/Modify

- CREATE: `packages/web/src/components/mobile/SwipeIndicators.tsx`
- CREATE: `packages/web/src/styles/swipe-indicators.css`
- MODIFY: `packages/web/src/App.tsx` (add component)
- MODIFY: `packages/web/src/styles/index.css` (import new CSS)

## Accessibility Considerations

- Arrows are decorative/hinting only, not interactive
- Use aria-hidden="true" since swipe is supplemental to Prev/Next buttons
- Ensure reduced-motion preference disables pulse animation
- pointer-events: none ensures they don't interfere with touch

## Acceptance Criteria

- Left/right arrow indicators appear on mobile viewports
- Arrows correctly hide at navigation boundaries (first/last phage)
- Arrows use correct z-index (below FAB/ControlDeck)
- Pulse animation plays on first appearance, then stops
- Indicators respect prefers-reduced-motion
- Arrows don't interfere with touch/swipe gestures
close_reason: Implemented SwipeIndicators component with CSS animations, integrated into App.tsx with isFirst/isLast boundary handling

title: Layer 2: Auxiliary Metabolic Gene (AMG) Pathway Mapper
description: Detect AMGs via HMMER vs curated profiles, map to KEGG reactions, estimate pathway flux gains via Delta-FBA in target hosts. Template models for common hosts, Δflux per pathway. Turns annotations into quantitative metabolic impact; surfaces hijacking strategies. Novelty: Medium-high, Pedagogical: High (stoichiometry, metabolic control).
notes:
## AUXILIARY METABOLIC GENE (AMG) FLUX POTENTIAL ANALYZER

**Full Implementation from Roadmap**

### Mathematical Foundations

**Flux Balance Analysis (FBA):**
```
Maximize: c^T × v (objective function, e.g., biomass)
Subject to: S × v = 0 (steady-state)
            v_min ≤ v ≤ v_max (flux bounds)
```

**Delta-FBA for AMG Impact:**
```
Δflux = v_with_AMG - v_without_AMG
%Gain = (v_with - v_without) / v_without × 100
```

### Complete TypeScript Implementation

- `HostModel` interface (metabolites, reactions, stoichiometry, objectives)
- `AMGDetection` with KO mapping, HMM scores, coverage
- `DeltaFBAResult` with pathway impacts and percent gains
- `PathwayImpact` (affected reactions, total flux change)
- `ECOLI_CORE_MODEL` with glycolysis, TCA, nucleotide synthesis
- `AMG_PROFILES` Map (psbA/D photosynthesis, nrdA/B nucleotide, thyX, mazG, phoH)
- `detectAMGs()` HMM-based detection
- `calculateDeltaFBA()` flux change estimation
- `analyzeAMGFluxPotential()` full analysis pipeline
- `formatAMGAnalysisForTUI()` display formatting

### TUI Features
- Metabolic Map with pathway flow visualization
- AMG positions marked with stars (★)
- Flux Impact Summary table with gain bars
- Host Comparison panel (Prochlorococcus, Synechococcus, E. coli, Bacillus)
- Total Δ Objective and compatibility scores
- Top Affected Pathways ranking
- [←/→] Switch AMG, [H] Switch host, [P] Pathway detail

### Implementation Stack
- Rust+WASM for LP solver (delta-FBA)
- HMMER precompute for AMG detection
- KEGG reaction mapping
- SQLite for pathway and AMG caches
- TS/Ink UI for metabolic flow visualization

Novelty: 8/10, Pedagogical: 9/10, Wow Factor: 8/10

title: EPIC: Truth-in-labeling — no fabricated result may look like analysis
description:
## Origin

Produced by an end-to-end reality check of the repository on 2026-09-01, which audited
all 46 analysis overlays in the web app against the computation actually behind them.
36 are genuinely derived from the loaded genome, the gene table, or the shipped SQLite
annotations. 10 are not. Several of those present fabricated or hash-derived numbers
with exactly the same visual authority as the real ones, and two do it underneath an
explicit green "REAL DATA" banner.

## Why this is the highest-priority epic in the project

Phage Explorer's stated purpose (README, "Why Phage Explorer Exists") is exploration and
education for researchers, plus phage-therapy candidate screening. A panel that looks
like analysis but is a hash of the phage name is worse than a missing feature: it
silently teaches something false, and it is indistinguishable from the 36 real overlays
sitting beside it in the same Analysis menu, with the same chrome, under the same
category label. A user cannot tell which is which without reading the source.

The project has already invested heavily in genuinely good analysis (dN/dS with
reverse-frame correctness, Gillespie tau-leaping resistance evolution, real Pfam-A hits
from PyHMMER, real ESM2 embeddings, WASM dot plots with JS parity tests). The fabricated
minority actively devalues that work, because a visitor who discovers one fake panel has
no reason to trust the other 36.

## The standard this epic establishes

Every number, chart, and badge displayed must be traceable to exactly one of:

1. the loaded genome sequence;
2. gene / annotation rows in phage.db;
3. a live external API response (NCBI Entrez, RCSB, SRA, Serratus);
4. a simulation whose parameters the user set, and whose synthetic nature is stated on
   the surface where results appear — not only in a tooltip, a doc, or a banner that
   scrolls off.

Anything else is either removed or carries a provenance badge at the point of display.
"Real", "heuristic", "simulated", and "demo" are four distinct provenances and the UI
must distinguish them everywhere, consistently.

## Definition of done

- No overlay displays a fabricated quantity without a visible provenance badge.
- The demo-driven overlays are either backed by real data or moved out of the plain
  "Analysis" category into a clearly marked group in both the Analysis Menu and the
  Command Palette, so the distinction is visible before opening.
- A test asserts the badge is present for every overlay classified heuristic/synthetic,
  so a future overlay cannot ship without one.

## Anti-goal

Do NOT resolve these by deleting features wholesale. Several of the offenders wrap
genuinely good math (the NMF/bootstrap in niche-network, the tree/skyline machinery in
phylodynamics) around a fabricated input. The fix is to feed them real data or label
them honestly, not to remove the mathematics.
close_reason: All ten children closed. Every overlay the audit found presenting fabricated output as analysis has been fixed at the source rather than relabelled: CRISPR mock spacers deleted after measuring that real ones do not hit this catalogue, environmental provenance containment made absent rather than zero, phylodynamics wired to real alignment-free distances with an e2e guard on its banner, niche network seeded per phage and moved out of Analysis, RNA structure stripped of its kcal/mol claim, virion stability's constant storage advice removed, packaging pressure given the physics its README promised. The class is closed structurally too: provenance is declared once in the registry and rendered by shared chrome in both entry points and the TUI, and a test fails if any overlay lacks a level.

title: CRISPR overlay is driven by a 6-mer mock spacer database presented as real
description:
## What is actually there

`packages/core/src/crispr.ts:37` carries the comment
`// Mock spacer database for demo purposes (in real app, this would be a DB query)`
followed by `MOCK_SPACERS = ['TGACGT','AACCGG','TTTGGG','CCCAAA','GGATCC','AAGCTT']` —
six 6-mers. These are scanned against the genome with `indexOf` (`crispr.ts:124-158`).

Consequences, all verified in source:

- A 6-mer recurs by chance roughly every 4 kb in a random sequence, so on a 48 kb genome
  the overlay reports dozens of "spacer hits" that are pure combinatorial noise.
- `host: 'E. coli K-12', // Mock host` (`crispr.ts:151`) is attached to every hit
  regardless of the phage's actual host, including the Mycobacterium, Streptomyces,
  Bacillus, Pseudomonas and marine phages in the catalog.
- `matchScore = 0.8 + seededUnit(...) * 0.2` and `strand` are derived from a string
  hash (`crispr.ts:145-146`), not from the sequence.
- `dominantType: 'II' // Simplified` (`crispr.ts:181`).
- The anti-CRISPR score falls back to `// Random perturbation for demo variety`
  (`crispr.ts:97-100`).

Only the hit positions and the PAM adjacency check touch real sequence data.

Nothing in either UI says any of this. `packages/web/src/components/overlays/CRISPROverlay.tsx:256-258,447-450`
renders the results as ordinary findings; the TUI equivalent is `packages/tui/src/components/CRISPROverlay.tsx`.
README markets it as "CRISPR Pressure — Spacer matching against mock host CRISPR arrays;
rates evolutionary pressure 0-10 scale" — the word "mock" appears in the README table but
never in the product.

## Why it matters

"Check Defense Arms Race for anti-CRISPR genes" is step 2 of the README's phage-therapy
candidate screening workflow. A therapy-screening workflow returning noise with a
confident 0-10 pressure score is the worst possible failure mode for this project.

## Options, in preference order

1. **Real spacers.** Ingest a real spacer set for the catalog's actual hosts from
   CRISPRCasdb (the NEW_IDEAS doc, idea 4 and Top-10 idea 2, specifies exactly this) and
   store it in phage.db as a new table at build time, keyed by host. Spacers are ~30 bp,
   so hits become meaningful. PAM-aware scoring already exists and can stay.
2. **Honest degradation.** If (1) is out of scope now, keep the machinery but gate it:
   show the overlay only when a real spacer set is present for the phage's host, and
   otherwise render an empty state that says which host data is missing.

Do not simply widen the mock k-mers — a longer fabricated spacer is still fabricated.

## Acceptance criteria

- No code path displays spacer hits derived from `MOCK_SPACERS`.
- Any residual heuristic carries the provenance badge from the badge bead.
- The host shown next to a hit is the phage's real host from phage.db, never a constant.
- A unit test asserts that a phage with no spacer data yields zero hits rather than
  chance matches.
close_reason: Measured first, then built. An exhaustive search of CRISPRCasdb spacers against all 24 catalogue genomes found 0 exact matches, 0 within 2 mismatches, 1 within 5 (P1, 4mm/32bp, chance in a 94kb genome). Option 1 is not available for this catalogue, so Option 2 shipped: MOCK_SPACERS and the hash-derived matchScore/strand/jitter are deleted, real spacers arrive as an argument, host comes from the spacer record, dominantType is counted rather than hardcoded to II, and both overlays name which host's data is missing instead of rendering zero pressure as a measurement. Registry provenance corrected from demo to heuristic. 30 unit tests including the required no-data test and a guard that rejects spacers shorter than 20bp.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Spacer data is available and measured, before anyone writes code

Option 1 in this bead (real spacers from CRISPRCasdb) is viable. Verified today,
not assumed:

- `https://crisprcas.i2bc.paris-saclay.fr/Home/DownloadFile?filename=spacer_34.zip`
  downloads in about 3 s (13 MB). It contains three FASTA files:
  `spacer_id.fsa` (353,377 spacers keyed by UUID, NO host information),
  `spacer_seqName.fsa` (14,111, keyed by host GenBank accession),
  `spacer_taxon.fsa` (6,528, keyed by NCBI taxon id).
- `spacer_taxon.fsa` is the usable one: it is the only file that joins directly
  to a host without a second lookup. Spacer lengths run 16-104 bp with the mode
  at 32 bp, against the 6 bp mock k-mers shipped today.

Coverage for this catalogue's actual hosts, counted from that file. Taxon ids
were resolved from NCBI E-utilities, not recalled:

    562     Escherichia coli            282 spacers
    83333   E. coli K-12                 25
    511145  E. coli K-12 MG1655          10
    37762   E. coli B                    11
    498388  E. coli C                     9
    28901   Salmonella enterica         582
    287     Pseudomonas aeruginosa       44
    100226  S. coelicolor A3(2)           1

That covers 19 of the 24 catalogue phages by host. Not covered at all:
Bacillus subtilis (phi29, SPbeta), Pseudomonas syringae (phi6),
Mycobacterium smegmatis (D29, L5), Pseudoalteromonas espejiana (PM2).
Note also that `Mycobacterium smegmatis` returns no taxon id from NCBI; the
species was renamed to `Mycolicibacterium smegmatis` and the lookup must use
that name or it silently finds nothing.

## What this means for the two options

Option 1 is possible for most of the catalogue and impossible for five phages.
So the work is BOTH options, not a choice between them: ingest real spacers
where they exist, and render the honest empty state of option 2 where they do
not. Five phages showing "no spacer data for Bacillus subtilis" is a correct
result, and far better than the current six 6-mers.

## Measure before building

The decisive number is not yet known and should be established first: do real
30-36 bp spacers actually hit these genomes? Exact matching is strict, and real
protospacer detection allows mismatches. Before any schema or pipeline work,
run the downloaded spacers against the 24 genomes at 0 and at up to 5 mismatches
and record the hit counts per phage. If the answer is near zero everywhere, the
deliverable is the honest empty state plus a recorded negative result, not a
spacer table nobody can use.

The archive is not committed anywhere; re-download it with the URL above.

title: Add a provenance badge primitive and apply it across all 46 analysis overlays
description:
## Purpose

The individual fixes in this epic remove the worst offenders. This bead makes the class of
defect structurally impossible to reintroduce, by giving every overlay a single, uniform,
required way to state where its numbers came from.

## Design

Add one primitive alongside the existing overlay primitives in
`packages/web/src/components/overlays/primitives/` (the design system documented in
`docs/overlay-design-system.md`), e.g. `OverlayProvenance`, with a closed set of levels:

| Level | Meaning | Example overlay |
|---|---|---|
| `measured` | computed from the loaded sequence or annotation rows | GC skew, dot plot, Pfam domains |
| `external` | fetched live from a named third-party API | 3D structure (RCSB), SRA geography |
| `heuristic` | a rule-based estimate, not a measurement | anti-CRISPR score, AMG keyword rules |
| `simulated` | a model the user parameterized | the 7 Simulation Hub entries |
| `demo` | synthetic input, not derived from the user's phage | niche network, if it stays synthetic |

The badge must render in the overlay header (always visible, not scrolled), carry an
accessible name, and honor the existing theme tokens and motion policy
(`docs/motion-policy.md`).

## Registry coupling

Add the provenance level to the overlay's entry in
`packages/web/src/keyboard/actionRegistry.ts` so the Analysis Menu and Command Palette can
show it *before* the user opens the overlay. This is what prevents the niche-network
situation, where the disclaimer only appears after opening.

## Enforcement

Add a test that enumerates every registered overlay id and fails if any lacks a
provenance level. This is the part that makes the fix durable — without it, overlay 47
ships unlabeled.

## Also apply to the TUI

The TUI has the same problem for the overlays it shares (CRISPR especially). Use the
equivalent single-line convention there.

## Acceptance criteria

- `OverlayProvenance` exists, is exported from the overlay primitives barrel, and is
  documented in `docs/overlay-design-system.md`.
- All 46 analysis overlays render a level.
- The Analysis Menu and Command Palette display the level.
- A test fails when an overlay id has no provenance level assigned.
close_reason: Blockers uhx4.7, uhx4.8 and uhx4.9 are closed. Badge applied via shared chrome: Overlay reads the level from actionRegistry and renders it in every overlay header, so overlay 47 is labelled on registration. Command Palette joins the Analysis Menu in showing it before the overlay opens. Documented in docs/overlay-design-system.md. TUI equivalent added and applied to its four non-measured overlays. Deliberate deviation: measured renders nothing, documented and test-enforced.
