comments.text:
## Stage 5: WebGPU Acceleration (HIGH PRIORITY)

### Goal
Leverage GPU compute shaders for massive parallelization of sequence analysis. WebGPU provides 10-100x speedup for suitable algorithms.

### Current State
A k-mer shader exists (`kmer.wgsl`) but is underutilized. Only used for k-mer spectrum analysis.

### New Shaders to Implement
1. **search.wgsl** - Parallel motif search
2. **gc_skew.wgsl** - Sliding window GC skew
3. **entropy.wgsl** - Windowed entropy computation
4. **edit_dist.wgsl** - Wavefront edit distance
5. **dotplot.wgsl** - Self-similarity matrix
6. **repeats.wgsl** - Palindrome/tandem detection

### WebGPU Availability
- Chrome 113+ (stable since April 2023)
- Edge 113+
- Firefox Nightly (behind flag)
- Safari 17+ (macOS 14+)

~70% of users have WebGPU support as of late 2024.

### Fallback Strategy
Always provide CPU fallback:
```typescript
async function computeGCSkew(seq: string): Promise<number[]> {
  if (gpuCompute.ready()) {
    return gpuCompute.runShader('gc_skew', seq);
  }
  return cpuComputeGCSkew(seq);
}
```

### Dependencies
- Requires Stage 4 (SharedArrayBuffer for GPU buffer sharing)
- GPUCompute.ts infrastructure exists

### Success Criteria
- Analysis operations 10-100x faster when GPU available
- Graceful fallback maintains functionality everywhere
- No visible difference in results

### Key Files
- packages/web/src/workers/gpu/GPUCompute.ts
- packages/web/src/workers/gpu/*.wgsl (new shaders)

title: A11y: LearnMenu keyboard + focus behavior
description:
### Background
`packages/web/src/components/LearnMenu.tsx` renders a popover menu but currently has limited keyboard behavior:
- no Esc-to-close
- no arrow-key navigation
- focus is not moved into the menu on open
- focus is not restored to the trigger on close

### Goal
Make LearnMenu behave like an accessible menu/popover:
- Enter/Space opens
- focus moves to the first item
- ArrowUp/ArrowDown roves through items
- Esc closes and returns focus to trigger
- Click-outside still closes

### Touchpoints

- Avoid focus traps: this is a popover, not a modal.

title: A11y: Overlays return focus on close + consistent Esc behavior
description:
### Background
The app uses an overlay system (`packages/web/src/components/overlays/*`). For accessibility and premium UX, overlays should:
- close on Escape (where appropriate)
- return focus to the element that opened them
- avoid leaving focus on a removed node

Some modal focus work exists historically, but the current overlay set should be audited end-to-end.

### Goal
Add consistent focus/keyboard behavior across overlays.

### Touchpoints
- `packages/web/src/components/overlays/Overlay.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/components/overlays/OverlayProvider.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/components/overlays/OverlayManager.tsx`
design:
Implementation notes:
- Store a reference to `document.activeElement` when opening an overlay and restore on close.
- Consider a small helper to avoid duplicating logic across overlays.
acceptance_criteria:
- Closing an overlay returns focus to the triggering control.
- Escape closes overlays that are dismissible.
- Focus is not trapped unless the overlay is modal by design.

title: Delete featureRegistry.ts and FullFeatureModal.tsx, 1590 lines reachable from nothing
description:
## What is dead

`packages/web/src/lib/featureRegistry.ts` (866 lines) and
`packages/web/src/components/controls/FullFeatureModal.tsx` (724 lines) --
1,590 lines whose only entry point is a modal that is exported from the controls
barrel and rendered nowhere.

The registry was also WRONG. It carried a `shortcuts?: string[]` on every entry:
a second, hand-maintained copy of the key map, of which roughly eighteen of
fifty-two disagreed with the real bindings (k-mer anomaly listed `V` against the
real Alt+J, HGT `Y` against Alt+H, dot plot `.` against Alt+O, diff `d` when
nothing registered it at all).

phage_explorer-v3wn.6 removed all 52 shortcut arrays, the unused
`getAllShortcuts` helper, and the two render sites, and added a test forbidding
the field's return. So the file can no longer mislead. It is still dead.

## Why deletion rather than wiring it up

Mounting the modal would not be an improvement. The Command Palette already
searches every action and reads its shortcuts from `actionRegistry.ts`, the
registry the app actually dispatches from. Mounting this would add a THIRD
discovery surface (Analysis Menu, Command Palette, All Features) fed by a
separate hand-maintained list, which is how the wrong shortcuts got there in the
first place.

If a browsable all-features view is genuinely wanted, build it from
`actionRegistry.ts` so it cannot drift. That is a different bead from this one.

## Why this needs the operator

AGENTS.md RULE 1 is absolute: no file or directory may be deleted without the
operator's explicit written approval, given in-session, with the exact command
restated before it runs. This bead exists to request that approval and record
the reasoning, not to pre-authorise it.

## The exact change requested

Delete two files:

    packages/web/src/lib/featureRegistry.ts
    packages/web/src/components/controls/FullFeatureModal.tsx

and remove the one export line that references the modal:

    packages/web/src/components/controls/index.ts:7

## Acceptance criteria

- Operator approval is recorded on this bead, quoting their exact authorising
  text, before anything is removed.
- After removal: `bun run check` exits 0 and the full suite passes, proving
  nothing else referenced them.
- A grep for `featureRegistry` and `FullFeatureModal` across the repo returns
  nothing outside this bead and the CHANGELOG entry.

## If the operator declines

That is a legitimate outcome. In that case add a header comment to both files
recording that they are intentionally unmounted and why, so the next reader does
not spend the time working it out again.

# Epic: Web Feature Parity & Mobile Excellence

## Executive Summary

This epic represents the strategic initiative to achieve full feature parity between the TUI and Web versions of Phage Explorer, while simultaneously establishing the Web version as a world-class mobile experience. The goal is not mere replication but intelligent adaptation—leveraging the unique strengths of each platform.

## Background & Rationale

### Current State Analysis

**TUI (Terminal UI) - 1100+ lines App.tsx**
- 50+ components, 40+ specialized analysis overlays
- 6 fully-implemented interactive simulations
- 56+ keyboard shortcuts across 7 categories
- Progressive experience system (novice→intermediate→power)
- Complete genomic analysis toolkit

**Web (Browser) - Current State**
- 43 overlay types defined, many incomplete
- 10 simulation types registered, visualizers partial
- 40+ keyboard shortcuts (good coverage)
- Mobile support exists but cell sizes problematic
- Canvas rendering works but needs optimization

### The Gap

1. **Mobile UX**: Cells too small for letters at default zoom; orientation changes not leveraged
2. **Analysis Overlays**: ~12 overlays incomplete or missing visualizations
3. **Simulation Visualizers**: 6 simulations need complete visualization components
4. **Progressive Disclosure**: Experience gating exists in state but not wired to UI
5. **3D Model**: Quality presets work but mobile-specific optimizations missing

## Strategic Goals

1. **100% Feature Parity**: Every TUI feature accessible via Web
2. **Mobile-First Excellence**: Touch-optimized, orientation-aware, readable at all sizes
3. **World-Class UX**: Discoverable, learnable, powerful
4. **Performance**: 60fps rendering, <100ms interactions, offline-capable
5. **Accessibility**: WCAG AA compliance, keyboard-only navigation, screen reader support

## Success Metrics

- All 40+ TUI overlays functional in Web
- All 6 simulations with complete visualizers
- Mobile NPS > 50 (Net Promoter Score)
- Lighthouse Performance > 90
- Time-to-Interactive < 3s on 3G

## Architecture Principles

1. **Shared Core**: Maximum code reuse via @phage-explorer/core
2. **Platform Adaptation**: TUI-optimized ≠ Web-optimized; adapt intelligently
3. **Progressive Enhancement**: Core features work without JS; enhanced with it
4. **Lazy Loading**: Load analysis algorithms on-demand via Web Workers
5. **Responsive First**: Design mobile, enhance for desktop

## Pillars of Work

### Pillar 1: Mobile Sequence Grid Excellence
Fix the current mobile grid issues and make it genuinely useful for genomic exploration.

### Pillar 2: Responsive & Orientation-Aware Layout  
Intelligent layout adaptation for portrait/landscape and all device sizes.

### Pillar 3: Complete Analysis Overlay Parity
Implement all 40+ TUI overlays with Web-optimized visualizations.

### Pillar 4: Simulation Visualizer Parity
Complete all 6 simulation visualizers with interactive controls.

### Pillar 5: Keyboard/Command Parity
Ensure all TUI hotkeys work in Web with proper conflict resolution.

### Pillar 6: Progressive Disclosure & UX Polish
Wire experience levels to UI, implement onboarding, feature tours.

### Pillar 7: 3D Visualization Parity
Mobile-optimized 3D with LOD, touch controls, quality presets.

### Pillar 8: Performance & Offline
Service worker optimization, lazy loading, cache strategies.

## Dependencies

- Existing @phage-explorer/core algorithms (complete)
- Existing @phage-explorer/state store (complete)  
- Web Workers infrastructure (exists, needs expansion)
- Canvas rendering system (exists, needs optimization)

## Timeline Estimate

Not providing time estimates per project guidelines. Work should be prioritized by impact and dependencies.

## Risk Factors

1. WebGL/WebGPU compatibility across mobile browsers
2. Memory constraints on older mobile devices
3. Touch gesture conflicts with browser gestures
4. IndexedDB storage limits for large genomes

title: Remove Cartoon 3D rendering mode
notes:
# Remove Cartoon 3D Rendering Mode

## Problem Statement

The "Cartoon" rendering mode is redundant with "Ribbon" mode and provides inferior visual results. Having two nearly-identical options confuses users and adds unnecessary UI complexity.

## Analysis

| Mode | What it renders | Visual style |
|------|-----------------|--------------|
| Ball-Stick | Atoms + bonds | Atomic detail |
| Cartoon | Backbone traces as tubes | Smooth tubes |
| Ribbon | Backbone traces as tubes | Smooth tubes |
| Surface | Solvent-accessible surface | Blob-like |

Cartoon and Ribbon both use `buildTubeFromTraces()` with nearly identical parameters:

**Cartoon (lines 169-177):**
```tsx
group = buildTubeFromTraces(
  data.backboneTraces,
  0.5,                              // radius
  qualityPreset.tubeRadialSegments,
  '#38bdf8',                        // color (sky blue)
  1,                                // opacity
  chainColors,
  qualityPreset.tubeMinSegments
);
```

**Ribbon (lines 179-188):**
```tsx
group = buildTubeFromTraces(
  data.backboneTraces,
  0.3,                              // radius (slightly thinner)
  Math.max(6, qualityPreset.tubeRadialSegments - 2),
  '#c084fc',                        // color (purple)
  0.9,                              // opacity (slightly transparent)
  chainColors,
  qualityPreset.tubeMinSegments
);
```

The only differences are:
- Tube radius (0.5 vs 0.3)
- Default color (sky blue vs purple)
- Opacity (1.0 vs 0.9)

These differences don't justify a separate mode.

## Solution

1. Remove 'cartoon' from the RenderMode type
2. Remove the Cartoon button from the UI toolbar
3. Remove the cartoon case from rebuildStructure switch
4. Optionally: Add thickness slider to Ribbon mode for users who want thicker tubes

## Files to Modify

**`/packages/web/src/components/Model3DView.tsx`:**
- Line 23: Remove 'cartoon' from RenderMode type
- Lines 169-177: Remove cartoon case
- Lines 531-543: Remove Cartoon button from toolbar

## UI Before/After

**Before:**
```
[Ball-Stick] [Cartoon] [Ribbon] [Surface]
```

**After:**
```
[Ball-Stick] [Ribbon] [Surface]
```

## Testing

- [ ] Cartoon button no longer appears
- [ ] Selecting modes still works correctly
- [ ] No TypeScript errors from removed type
- [ ] Default mode (ball) still works

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Cartoon mode completely removed from codebase
- [ ] UI shows only 3 render modes
- [ ] No console errors or warnings
- [ ] Ribbon mode remains fully functional

title: Feature: Mobile Touch UX Overhaul - Touch-First Redesign

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
# Mobile Touch UX Overhaul - Touch-First Redesign

## The Problem

The mobile experience has fundamental anti-patterns that make the app frustrating to use on touch devices:

1. **Touch targets too small** - Many interactive elements are < 44px (Apple minimum)
2. **Hover-dependent interactions** - GeneMapCanvas tooltips require mouse hover
3. **Accidental gestures** - Low swipe threshold (80px) causes unintended navigation
4. **Broken landscape mode** - Control Deck takes 50% of viewport
5. **Poor discoverability** - Control Deck appears suddenly with no affordance

## Impact

- ~60% of users on mobile/tablet (estimate based on analytics)
- High bounce rate on mobile devices
- Negative reviews citing "unusable on phone"
- Accessibility violations (WCAG 2.5.5 Target Size)

## Current State Analysis

### Touch Targets (mobile-overrides.css:61)
```css
/* Current - too small */
.btn-sm { min-height: 32px; min-width: 32px; }

/* Should be */
.btn-sm { min-height: 44px; min-width: 44px; }
```

### GeneMapCanvas (GeneMapCanvas.tsx:46-90)
- Uses `onMouseMove` for hover detection
- Tooltip positioned with `fixed` (fragile on mobile)
- No touch event handlers
- Click-to-navigate requires precise aim

### Control Deck (control-deck.css:28)
- Fixed 140px height regardless of viewport
- On iPhone SE landscape: 140/320 = 44% of viewport
- "Tools" tab opens Command Palette (confusing naming)

### Swipe Threshold (App.tsx:274-275)
- Horizontal: 80px (too low)
- Vertical tolerance: 60px (too permissive)
- Accidental swipes while scrolling list

## Solution Architecture

### 1. Touch Target Audit & Fix
Systematically ensure all interactive elements meet minimum 44x44px:
- Buttons (including badge buttons, compact mode)
- List items (entire row should be tappable)
- Gene map segments (expand hit area)
- Overlay close buttons

### 2. Touch-Friendly Gene Tooltips
Replace mouse hover with:
- Long-press to show tooltip (300ms delay)
- Tap to navigate + brief tooltip flash
- Bottom sheet for detailed info on mobile

### 3. Control Deck Improvements
- Dynamic height based on viewport (max 40% landscape, 50% portrait)
- Clear visual affordance (subtle "swipe up for more" hint)
- Rename "Tools" to something clearer
- Add drag handle for resize

### 4. Gesture Threshold Tuning
- Increase swipe threshold to 120px minimum
- Reduce vertical tolerance to 40px
- Add velocity detection (fast swipes count, slow drags don't)

### 5. Landscape Mode Fix
- Control Deck collapses to single-row in landscape
- Expand on tap to show full controls
- Or: Move to side panel in landscape

## Design Guidelines

**Touch targets:**
- Minimum 44x44px visual + interactive area
- 8px minimum spacing between targets
- Use padding to expand hit area (not just visual size)

**Gestures:**
- Single-tap: primary action
- Long-press (300ms): secondary action (tooltip, context menu)
- Swipe: navigation (high threshold, velocity-aware)
- Pinch: zoom (if applicable)

**Feedback:**
- Immediate visual response on touch (< 100ms)
- Haptic feedback on iOS (if available)
- Touch ripple effect on Android-style

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All touch targets >= 44x44px
- [ ] Gene map works with touch (tap + long-press)
- [ ] Control Deck < 40% viewport in landscape
- [ ] No accidental phage changes from list scrolling
- [ ] Works on iPhone SE (smallest common device)

notes:
## PHYLODYNAMIC TRAJECTORY EXPLORER

**Full Implementation from Roadmap**

### Concept
For dated accessions, build time-scaled trees and visualize rate shifts, skyline Ne, and rapidly evolving loci with selection signals.

### How to Build

**Time-Scaled Tree:**
- Lightweight BEAST-like approximation in Rust+WASM
- Rate-smoothed neighbor-joining
- Treetime-style root-to-tip regression
- Infer molecular clock rate

**Skyline Population Dynamics:**
- Coalescent skyline via interval counts
- Compute effective population size Ne(t)
- Credible bands from bootstrap or MCMC-lite

**Selection Mapping:**
- dN/dS per branch/window (FEL-like fast approximation)
- Map to genome positions
- Highlight rapidly evolving loci

**Data Ingest:**
- Accession dates + sequences
- Multiple sequence alignment
- Cache alignments and trees in SQLite

### TUI Features
- ASCII time-scaled tree with branch lengths
- Side skyline plot showing Ne over time
- Genome heat strip for dN/dS values
- Cursor on tree highlights corresponding loci
- Rate shift annotations on branches
- Press 't' to toggle tree/skyline focus

### Why It's Good
- Shows evolutionary tempo and population expansions
- Connects time to genome changes
- Identifies selection hotspots
- Tracks viral evolution in real time

### Implementation Stack
- Rust+WASM for clock/regression/selection calculations
- TS/Ink for tree and skyline rendering
- SQLite caches for alignments and trees
- ASCII tree with Unicode box-drawing characters

Novelty: 9/10, Pedagogical: 9/10, Wow Factor: 9/10

# Verify All Phages Have 3D Model Support

## Problem Statement

The user reported that "Lambda phage and other important critical phages" are missing from the web interface. This needs investigation and verification.

## Current State

### Phage Catalog
**File:** `/packages/data-pipeline/src/phage-catalog.ts`

The catalog includes 12 phages with PDB IDs:

| Phage | Accession | PDB IDs |
|-------|-----------|---------|
| Lambda | NC_001416.1 | 7VI9, 8K35 |
| T4 | NC_000866.4 | 5VF3 |
| T7 | NC_001604.1 | 3J4G |
| PhiX174 | NC_001422.1 | 2BPA |
| MS2 | NC_001417.2 | 2MS2 |
| M13 | NC_003287.2 | 2MJZ |
| P22 | NC_002371.2 | 5UU5 |
| Phi29 | NC_011048.1 | 1MN8 |
| Mu | NC_000929.1 | 4FCY, 1WRU, 5YVQ |
| Phi6 | NC_003714.1 | 4BTG |
| SPbeta | NC_001884.1 | 5Y24, 6HP7, 5XYB |
| T5 | NC_005859.1 | 8ZVI, 6OMC, 5TJT |

Lambda IS in the catalog. So why isn't it showing?

## Investigation Tasks

### 1. Check Database Build
Verify the phage.db contains all 12 phages:
```bash
bun run build:db
sqlite3 phage.db "SELECT name, pdb_ids FROM phages ORDER BY name"
```

### 2. Check Web Repository Query
**File:** `/packages/web/src/db/SqlJsRepository.ts`

Verify `listPhages()` returns all phages:
```typescript
const result = this.db.exec(`
  SELECT id, name, accession, family, ...
  FROM phages
  ORDER BY name
`);
```

### 3. Check 3D Model Loading
For each phage, verify:
1. `phage.pdbIds` array is populated
2. First PDB ID resolves to a valid RCSB URL
3. Structure loads without error

### 4. RCSB Availability
Some older PDB entries may have been superseded or removed. Check each PDB ID:
```bash
for pdb in 7VI9 8K35 5VF3 3J4G 2BPA 2MS2 2MJZ 5UU5 1MN8 4FCY 4BTG 5Y24 8ZVI; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} $pdb\n" https://files.rcsb.org/download/$pdb.pdb
done
```

## Potential Issues

### Issue 1: Database Not Rebuilt
If `bun run build:db` hasn't been run after catalog updates, the database may be stale.

### Issue 2: JSON Parsing
PDB IDs are stored as JSON in SQLite. Check parsing:
```typescript
pdbIds: safeJsonParse<string[]>(phage.pdbIds, []),
```

### Issue 3: Web App Cache
IndexedDB may have cached an older database version.

## Remediation Steps

1. **Rebuild database:**
   ```bash
   rm phage.db
   bun run build:db
   ```

2. **Clear web app cache:**
   - Open DevTools > Application > IndexedDB
   - Delete phage-explorer database
   - Reload

3. **Verify all phages load:**
   - Each phage should appear in the list
   - Each phage with PDB IDs should show 3D model

## Testing Checklist

- [ ] Lambda phage appears in the list
- [ ] Lambda 3D model loads (PDB 7VI9 or 8K35)
- [ ] All 12 catalog phages appear
- [ ] All 12 phages have working 3D models
- [ ] No console errors during structure loading

## Definition of Done

- [ ] All 12 catalog phages visible in web UI
- [ ] All phages with PDB IDs load 3D structures
- [ ] Any missing/broken PDB IDs replaced with alternatives
- [ ] Database rebuild script works correctly

title: Fix O(n²) string concatenation in getSequenceWindow

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Fix O(n²) String Concatenation

### Problem
In `packages/db-runtime/src/bun-repository.ts` lines 213-215:
```typescript
let fullSeq = '';
for (const chunk of result) {
  fullSeq += chunk.sequence;
}
```

JavaScript string concatenation in a loop is **O(n²)** because strings are immutable - each += creates a new string and copies all previous content.

For T4 phage (169kb genome, 17 chunks of 10kb each):
- First concat: copy 10kb
- Second: copy 20kb  
- Third: copy 30kb
- ... 17th: copy 170kb
- Total: ~1.5MB of memory churn, many allocations

### Solution
Use array join which is O(n):
```typescript
const fullSeq = result.map(chunk => chunk.sequence).join('');
```

This creates array pointers, then single final string - one allocation.

### Files to Fix
1. `packages/db-runtime/src/bun-repository.ts` (lines 213-215)
2. `packages/web/src/db/SqlJsRepository.ts` (similar pattern)

### Impact
- 10-100x faster for large genomes (T4, SPbeta at 134kb, T5 at 122kb)
- Reduced GC pressure from fewer allocations
- Especially noticeable on rapid scrolling where getSequenceWindow called frequently

### Testing
1. Open T4 phage (largest genome)
2. Rapidly scroll through entire genome
3. Should be noticeably smoother

### Why Priority 0 (Critical)?
This is in the hot path - called on EVERY scroll event for sequence data. The accumulated cost is massive for usability.

description:
# Phase 5: Advanced Features (Target: Weeks 9-11)

## Purpose
Implement computationally intensive analyses and leverage web-only capabilities not available in the TUI.

## Why This Matters
These features differentiate the web version from the TUI. WebGPU enables massive parallelism impossible in terminals. WebRTC enables collaboration impossible in local apps. Video export enables sharing impossible without GUIs.

## Deliverables
1. **Advanced Analysis Overlays** - K-mer, module detection, selection pressure
2. **WebGPU Acceleration** - GPU k-mer counting, parallel analysis
3. **Collaborative Sessions** - WebRTC-based real-time collaboration
4. **Export Capabilities** - Clipboard, FASTA, video, file system
5. **Matrix Rain Effect** - Background visual effect

## Advanced Analyses

### K-mer Anomaly Cartography
- High-resolution k-mer frequency deviation
- Windowed analysis across genome
- Anomaly highlighting

### Module Detection
- Functional gene clustering
- Operon boundary prediction
- Regulatory region identification

### Selection Pressure (dN/dS)
- Synonymous vs non-synonymous ratio
- Per-gene and sliding window
- Evolutionary pressure visualization

### Transcription Flow
- Promoter strength mapping
- Terminator detection
- Transcription unit visualization

## Web-Only Features

### WebGPU Compute (Feature Flagged)
```typescript
// GPU-accelerated k-mer counting
// 10-100x speedup for large sequences
async function gpuKmerCount(sequence, k): Map<string, number>
```

### WebRTC Collaboration
```typescript
class CollaborationManager {
  createSession(): Promise<string>  // Returns session ID
  joinSession(id): Promise<void>    // Join existing session
  broadcastStateChange(change): void // Sync with peers
}
```

### Export Capabilities
| Format | API Used |
|--------|----------|
| Rich clipboard | Clipboard API (HTML + plain) |
| FASTA | Clipboard/File System Access |
| Video | WebCodecs |
| Files | File System Access API |

### Matrix Rain
- DNA/amino acid characters
- Background decoration during loading
- Configurable density and speed

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All advanced analyses complete in reasonable time (<30s for 100kb)
- [ ] Progress streaming shows incremental results
- [ ] Results match TUI implementation exactly
- [ ] WebGPU provides measurable speedup (where supported)
- [ ] Collaboration sessions work between two browsers
- [ ] All export formats produce valid output

## Browser Support Matrix
| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---------|--------|---------|--------|
| WebGPU | ✅ | 🚧 | 🚧 |
| File System Access | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| WebCodecs | ✅ | 🚧 | ❌ |
| WebRTC | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

## Risks & Mitigations
- **Risk**: WebGPU not widely available
  - **Mitigation**: Feature flag, graceful fallback to WASM
- **Risk**: File System Access limited support
  - **Mitigation**: Fall back to download/input elements
- **Risk**: Collaboration signaling complexity
  - **Mitigation**: Use simple edge function, not full TURN server

## Dependencies
- Phase 4 (worker orchestration for heavy compute)
- Phase 3 (overlays to display results)
- Edge functions for collaboration signaling

title: Implement PostProcessPipeline WebGL2 Effects
description:
## NEW DIRECTION: Wire Up WebGL2 + Enhance with Libretro CRT Shaders

### Background

The existing `PostProcessingPipeline.ts` (313 lines) has a solid WebGL2 foundation:
- Full-screen quad rendering
- Texture upload from canvas
- Scanlines, chromatic aberration, bloom, vignette, noise

But it's **never wired up** - `PostProcessingCanvas.tsx` exists but is never rendered.

### New Goal

1. **Wire up the existing pipeline** - Render PostProcessingCanvas in AppShell
2. **Enhance with libretro-style CRT shaders** inspired by `slang-shaders/crt/shaders/newpixie`

### Effects to Add (from newpixie-crt)

| Effect | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Screen Curvature** | Barrel distortion simulating CRT geometry |
| **Shadow Mask** | Phosphor dot pattern overlay |
| **Rolling Scanlines** | Animated horizontal refresh lines |
| **Ghosting** | Temporal color bleeding |
| **Film Tone Mapping** | Filmic curve for color grading |

### Implementation Plan

1. **Phase 1: Wire Up** (Quick win)
   - Import PostProcessingCanvas into AppShell
   - Connect to settings (scanlines, bloom, aberration toggles)
   - Verify basic effects work

2. **Phase 2: Enhanced Shaders** (libretro-inspired)
   - Add curvature uniform + barrel distortion
   - Add shadow mask pattern
   - Add ghosting via temporal buffer
   - Add proper multi-pass bloom

3. **Phase 3: Settings UI**
   - Add sliders for: curvature, scanline intensity, bloom strength
   - Preset modes: "Subtle", "Classic CRT", "NewPixie", "Off"

### Files to Modify

- `packages/web/src/components/layout/AppShell.tsx` - Add PostProcessingCanvas
- `packages/web/src/rendering/PostProcessingPipeline.ts` - Enhance shaders
- `packages/web/src/components/overlays/SettingsOverlay.tsx` - Add CRT controls
- `packages/web/src/store/createWebStore.ts` - Add CRT settings state

### Reference

- Libretro slang-shaders: https://github.com/libretro/slang-shaders
- Specifically: `crt/shaders/newpixie/newpixie-crt.slang`

### Why This Matters

The retro CRT aesthetic is core to Phage Explorer's visual identity. Proper WebGL2 effects will be much more impressive than CSS overlays and enable future shader-based visualizations.

tsconfig includes a file that does not exist and the WASM ambient types are stale
description:
## Two small drifts in the WASM package's type surface

**1. Phantom include.** `tsconfig.json:41` includes
`packages/wasm-compute/test-wasm.ts`. The file does not exist. It is harmless today but
misleads anyone reading the project's compilation surface, and would silently start
compiling something unexpected if a file with that name reappeared.

**2. Hand-written ambient module is out of date.**
`packages/wasm-compute/index.d.ts` is a hand-maintained
`declare module '@phage/wasm-compute'` block. Compared against the generated
`packages/wasm-compute/pkg/wasm_compute.d.ts`, it is missing at least: `cgr_counts`,
`hilbert_rgba`, `compute_windowed_entropy_acgt`, `pca_power_iteration_f32`,
`compute_micro_runs`, `init_panic_hook`, `CgrCountsResult`, `PCAResultF32`, and
`Vector3`.

Several of those are actively used at runtime (`cgr_counts` and `hilbert_rgba` from
`packages/web/src/workers/hilbert.worker.ts`; `pca_power_iteration_f32` from
`packages/core/src/analysis/pca.ts`), which means those call sites are typed loosely or via
casts rather than against the real signatures. That weakens the ABI guarantees
`docs/WASM_ABI_SPEC.md` describes.

## The fix

- Remove the phantom include.
- Stop hand-maintaining the ambient declarations: re-export the generated `.d.ts` instead,
  so the types cannot drift from the artifact. If a hand-written layer is genuinely needed
  (e.g. to narrow the wasm-bindgen types), generate it and check the generation in CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- `tsc --noEmit` compiles with no reference to a nonexistent file.
- The declared surface of `@phage/wasm-compute` matches the built package, verified in CI.
